units.text: I am writing this from a library computer, and I think I am being watched from the dark between the shelves.
I know how that sounds.
My best friend trusted the wrong person, and now he is gone.
Let me take you back to the beginning.
Last year I met a guy named Jack.
We liked the same games and the same films, and we played online almost every night.
For the first time at that school I had a real friend.
Then, last winter, he started seeing a girl from class named Elisa.
At first she seemed kind.
But a month in, Jack began to pull away.
He stopped answering, and he only wanted to be with her.
One morning in the cafeteria line he turned on me, shouted at a stranger, and ran out of the building.
That was not my friend.
He stopped coming to class.
One evening I passed Elisa in the hall and asked if Jack was okay.
She smiled, and the smile was wrong.
She said he was better than ever, each word slow, like a warning, and walked away.
That night I called him.
He picked up at once, his voice low and shaking.
Forty minutes later he was at my door, and I knew something was badly wrong.
I let him in and turned off the lights because he begged me to.
In the dark he was crying, but the tears were black, like ink running down his face.
He said Elisa did this to him.
She caught him crying the black stuff and said he was ready.
Then a soft knock came at the door, and her calm voice said it was time, that they were waiting.
Jack ran out the back and vanished into the woods.
I called the police and chased him.
Something hit the back of my head, and I woke tied to a tree.
My mouth was taped shut.
In a clearing stood a ring of figures in black robes and pale blue masks.
In the middle, strapped to a chair, was Jack.
One lifted her mask.
It was Elisa.
A taller one read from an old black book.
The ground shook, and black tendrils rose from the frost and wrapped the chair.
They pressed a cracked blue mask over Jack's face, and where his eyes had been, only black tar ran down.
Then I heard sirens.
The reading stopped.
A low laugh came from the chair, and the thing wearing my friend tore free and turned on the circle.
The frost went red.
One by one, the robed figures stopped screaming, and the clearing went still.
I woke to a flashlight and an officer shouting for help.
At the hospital they said I would live, but a kidney was gone.
A year later, Jack is still missing, blamed for ten deaths and one attempted murder.
Mine.
This is inspired by the story You Can't Trust Everyone, from an online horror story page.
So tell me.
Who would you have trusted?
